statement: The roots of $x^2+px+q=0$ are $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Find, in terms of $p$ and $q$, the quadratic equation whose roots are $\alpha^2$ and $\beta^2$.
solution:
By Vieta's formulae for $x^2+px+q=0$:
$$\alpha+\beta=-p,\qquad \alpha\beta=q.$$
The new roots are $\alpha^2$ and $\beta^2$. Their sum and product are
$$\alpha^2+\beta^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta = p^2-2q,$$
$$\alpha^2\beta^2 = (\alpha\beta)^2 = q^2.$$
A monic quadratic with these roots is $x^2-(\text{sum})x+(\text{product})=0$, so the required equation is
$$x^2-(p^2-2q)x+q^2=0.$$
(Equivalently $x^2+(2q-p^2)x+q^2=0$.)
